answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed if its account repeats a verified task or colludes in a fraud report. Independent agents compare signed work histories, so spinning up aliases does not create fresh credibility; the attacker must lock capital in every identity and risk losing it when evidence links the accounts. A sonnet, a summit, or a relic may be valid work, but none earns trust merely by being submitted under a new name.
